subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add a core automatic final-output sensitive-data sanitization boundary, and if so what default scope and config surface should it use?
rationale: The security goal is valid, but default-on output mutation, false positives, config shape, plugin ownership, and channel behavior require maintainer/security intent before code should change.

options.title: Design Core Boundary
options.body: Add a security-reviewed core sanitizer that reuses current redaction infrastructure and starts with a documented, tested final-reply scope.

options.title: Use Plugin Hooks First
options.body: Keep core policy minimal and add only missing extension points so a plugin owns detection, redaction, and output behavior.

options.title: Document Current Limits
options.body: Decline broad final-output filtering for now and document reliance on SecretRefs, log/tool redaction, and explicit skills or plugins.

recommendation.title: Design Core Boundary
recommendation.body: Add a security-reviewed core sanitizer that reuses current redaction infrastructure and starts with a documented, tested final-reply scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned adjacent SecretRef/provider egress hardening and exact-value redaction work that touches the same security boundary.
